shard_query: Do candidate third-party visual-effect libraries justify adoption in the core product?
questions_answered: What evidence-backed product, interaction, visual, accessibility, and technical design should define a best-in-class native macOS ADHD-aware focus coach?

key_findings.claim: Pow, Vortex, Inferno, and Glur are all MIT-licensed and declare macOS 12 or newer, but their maintenance and dependency profiles differ materially.

key_findings.claim: Vortex, Inferno, and Glur declare no package dependencies, while Pow declares an exact SnapshotPreviews-iOS dependency even though its preview integration is disabled by default.

key_findings.notes: SPM can still fetch declared packages even when a target dependency is conditionally unused, so Pow adds supply-chain surface.

key_findings.claim: None of the four audited repositories contains an integrated Reduce Motion or Reduce Transparency policy; Praxodoro must gate third-party effects at its own design-system boundary.

key_findings.notes: Absence of an integrated policy is not a defect in a low-level effect library, but it matters at product integration.

key_findings.claim: The core UI should have zero mandatory visual-effect dependencies; prototype native SwiftUI and Metal first, then consider Vortex for rare particles or selectively port a small audited Inferno shader with attribution.

key_findings.notes: Final adoption requires runtime frame, energy, and memory measurements on target hardware.

next_queries: Run a visual prototype with native MeshGradient plus one custom Metal background before adding packages.
Benchmark Vortex and a copied Inferno shader under Reduce Motion and low-power mode.
Review source attribution requirements for any copied shader before release.
summary: The audited libraries are legitimate and current enough to prototype, but none should define the core visual architecture. Native APIs minimize supply-chain and accessibility risk; Vortex or a small attributed Inferno shader are the strongest bounded candidates after measurement.
